title: Given daily prices, maximise profit from buying and selling a stock, covering the single-transaction case and the unlimited-transaction case. Explain both algorithms, the operations, the complexity, and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (Single and Multiple Transactions)
keyPoints: Single transaction: track the minimum price seen so far and the best profit of selling at each day's price
Unlimited transactions: sum every positive day-over-day gain, capturing each upward move
Both run in a single linear pass with O(n) time and O(1) space
The single-transaction running minimum guarantees the buy day precedes the sell day
Summing positive daily gains is mathematically equivalent to buying at every trough and selling at every peak
The k-transaction and cooldown variants require state-machine dynamic programming

s1_definition.oneliner: One trade tracks the min and best sell; many trades sum every positive daily gain.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Single transaction** – track the lowest price seen so far (best buy point) and the best profit of selling today at that minimum. One pass, O(1) space.
- **Unlimited transactions** – sum every positive difference between consecutive days; each gain represents a profitable buy-sell pair. One pass, O(1) space.
- **Running minimum** – guarantees the buy day always precedes the sell day without comparing every pair.
- **Greedy insight** – capturing every positive daily step is equivalent to buying at each local trough and selling at each local peak.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India trading desk reviews a security's daily prices and wants the maximum profit: either from one clean buy-and-sell, or from many back-to-back trades capturing every rise.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Single Transaction:
  Prices:  7   1   5   3   6   4
  Min:     7   1   1   1   1   1
  Profit:  0   0   4   2   5   3
  Best:    0   0   4   4   5   5  -> answer: 5

  Unlimited Transactions:
  Prices:  7   1   5   3   6   4
  Diffs:      -6  +4  -2  +3  -2
  Sum positives: 4 + 3 = 7  -> answer: 7

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Single:    buy at day 1 (1), sell day 4 (6) │
  │  Unlimited: buy 1 sell 5 (+4), buy 3 sell 6 (+3) │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock is a family of problems, and the two base cases are both greedy single passes. For a single transaction, I track the lowest price seen so far and compute the profit of selling at each day's price against that minimum, keeping the best. The running minimum guarantees the buy day is always before the sell day.

For unlimited transactions, the maximum profit is the sum of every positive day-over-day difference. Capturing each upward step is mathematically equivalent to buying at every local trough and selling at every local peak. Both algorithms are O(n) time and O(1) space with no table at all.

The harder variants, limiting to at most K transactions or adding a cooldown day, require state-machine dynamic programming that tracks holding and not-holding states. These build on the same intuition but need a proper DP table.

At the National Bank of India, the trading desk used the running-minimum scan for the single-trade figure and the positive-gain sum for the unlimited figure, both fast enough for real-time dashboards over daily price series.

Remember one sentence: for one trade track the running minimum and best sell; for unlimited trades sum every positive daily gain; both are O(n) greedy passes.
